prompt: The best way to provide enough homes in large cities is to build tall apartment blocks. To what extent do you agree or disagree with this statement?
essay:
It is argued that the solution to the housing crisis is to build big blocks with lots of apartments, reaching a higher number of houses. In my opinion, building these high condominiums can provide enough homes in big metropolises, but with regulations. By making a high number of apartments, the offer increases , and it gives more options to people in need, and it is a good way to make the most of the area in big cities.

On the one hand, increasing the number of condominiums in a big city is directly related to a rise in supply in that sector. Raising the supply means making a better balance between supply and demand, making the prices fall , and by this giving more opportunities. It is a good solution to the problem because it is related to high housing prices in big cities. For example, Carlos III University in Madrid  made a study regarding the housing crisis in Spain nowadays and found that a possible solution is to increase the supply by building at least  1 million houses around the country.

On the other hand, big metropolises have issues with space because there are many more people than houses , so not everyone can fit in these places. It is known that these kinds of cities have empty spaces in the outskirts that can be used to build these high condominiums. Moreover, if this kind of construction is made in the metropolis, the space is used in a way that many more people fit, even if it is not in the centre, which improves the efficiency of city planning. For instance, the “Comunidad de Madrid” in 2022  built three one-hundred-and-fifty-meter apartment blocks near  the airport to help with the increase in population in the city.

Overall, building these kinds of blocks in a big capital  helps to provide enough homes for everyone by increasing the supply and decreasing housing prices and finally, with the optimisation of the space to raise the capacity of the capital.
